primary.purpose: The spot colour. Seed --primary-base #1c2f9e darkened 8% (#18298d), 10.7-11.8:1 as text on every light surface. Dark mode re-lights the seed (lightness ~78%, seed hue and chroma held) to #7aa2ff rather than tinting it toward white. Links, focus, current/active state, interpuncts, dots, counts, the one filled button, the plate.

secondary.purpose: Seed --secondary-base #85253a. Data only: chart series slot 2, corpus comparison, the publication type dot. Dark: mixed 30% toward white. Never UI chrome.

surface.purpose: The page: body paints --surface, one flat sheet. Page blocks carry no fill of their own.

background.purpose: Still published for consumers; the page no longer paints it.

warning.purpose: oklch(63.5% 0.18 60). Also --type-document and --type-entity-organisations, which render as solid dots, so it is calibrated as a non-text mark: 3:1 on all four light surfaces (3.51 / 3.39 / 3.31 / 3.20). Not a text colour at any lightness that stays amber.

info.purpose: Teal since 2.33, moved off the blue it shared with the new primary. Notices, AI provenance, the audiovisual and Personnes dots.

ink-subtle.purpose: Third-tier text: quiet chrome and secondary metadata.

ink-on-pastel.purpose: The one text ink used on tinted status grounds.

ink-on-primary.purpose: Text and icons on a --primary fill (filled buttons, submits, add/remove-value hover, checked tick). White in light (12.06:1 on --primary); warm dark ink in dark mode, where white on the re-lit blue is 2.49:1 and the dark ink reads 7.92 / 9.99 / 6.29:1 rest / hover / pressed. Never a hardcoded --white.

success-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.04 152). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(50% 0.13 152).

warning-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.05 60). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(55% 0.16 60) — a darker, more saturated base than the foreground hue, struck so the lamplit plate does not wash out.

error-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.04 25). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(50% 0.18 25) — same reasoning as the warning ground.

info-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.025 200). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(50% 0.10 200).

display.purpose: The homepage hero heading, white on the plate, at >=1024px (--text-3xl / --text-4xl below). The masthead wordmark is the same voice at 1.1875rem / 1.5rem.

headline.purpose: h1; the --text-3xl clamp below 768px. The plate page head title is Besley 800 white, 1.875rem / --text-3xl / --text-4xl; an off-plate page title is the h1.title section head, Besley 800 1.875rem on a 2px ink rule.

subhead.purpose: h2; 1.875rem below 768px. Never painted in primary.

title.purpose: h3 and ledger-row item titles; 1.5rem below 768px.

section-head.purpose: In-record section heads (How to cite, Linked resources, Archived web page): h2 sized by the section-head mixin, --ink-strong, --tracking-display, opened by the 2px ink rule. Never primary.

body.purpose: UI text, line-height 1.6, old-style proportional figures; paragraphs at 1.7.

body-serif.purpose: Article full text and ledes at line-height 1.7; long AI and OCR prose one step up at 1.1875rem. Short prose flows into balanced columns from 1024px.

label.purpose: Metadata dts in --ink, form labels, disclosure toggles, hero stat captions, breadcrumbs. Public Sans, untracked, never uppercase.

dateline.purpose: The two homes of tracked uppercase, both in --font-condensed (Fira Sans Condensed 500/600, falling back to the Public Sans stack): TYPE · PUBLISHER · DATE, carousel datelines and news date headers at +0.08em; the nav strip and drawer at +0.04em. In IwacVisualizations: chart axes, legends, tooltips. Carries every transliteration glyph, ʿ included. 11px (--text-2xs) is the absolute floor.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Flat since 2.33: published as a transparent zero shadow (not none, so composed box-shadow lists stay valid) because both modules still consume the name.

shadows.name: shadow-sm

shadows.name: shadow-md

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: The one real elevation: overlays that float over the page and dismiss (drawer, menus, language switcher, tooltips, annotation popovers, typeahead). Dark is struck from pure black at higher alpha. Declared in BOTH theme mixins.

shadows.name: panel-shadow
shadows.purpose: Flat since 2.33: published as a transparent zero shadow (not none, so composed box-shadow lists stay valid) because both modules still consume the name.

shadows.name: glow-xs
shadows.purpose: Flat since 2.33: published as a transparent zero shadow (not none, so composed box-shadow lists stay valid) because both modules still consume the name.

shadows.name: glow-sm
shadows.purpose: Flat since 2.33: published as a transparent zero shadow (not none, so composed box-shadow lists stay valid) because both modules still consume the name.

shadows.name: glow-md
shadows.purpose: Flat since 2.33: published as a transparent zero shadow (not none, so composed box-shadow lists stay valid) because both modules still consume the name.

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: THE default focus indicator, paired with outline-offset: 2px. Declared in BOTH theme mixins. White on the plate.

shadows.name: ring-focus
shadows.purpose: Box-shadow ring: the input focus ring (with a primary border) and the exception for controls an outline would be clipped on. Always with outline: 2px solid transparent.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Color/border state changes; the bare time for transition-duration / animation-duration.

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: --duration-fast on the house curve. Color/border state changes.

motion.name: transition-base
motion.purpose: --duration-base on the house curve. Default transitions.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: --duration-slow on the house curve. No bounce, no elastic. A literal duration fails npm run check:tokens.

typeMap.purpose: Fixed semantic map for resource types and the five index (entity) types, rendered as dots on outlined square chips. Article = the spot blue, publication = claret, audiovisual = teal info; Personnes / Lieux / Organisations reuse info / success / warning; Sujets and Evenements alias --series-5 (purple) and --series-9 (magenta). Declared in BOTH theme blocks. Every slot clears 3:1 on all four surfaces of its theme.

categoricalSeries.purpose: The theme-owned categorical chart palette, consumed by IwacVisualizations. Slots 1-2 alias --primary/--secondary (blue / claret) and flip with the theme; slots 3-20 are literals, independent per theme, tuned in lightness only so every slot clears 3:1 on all four surfaces of its theme (asserted by npm run check:tokens). 2.33 re-picked the slots that crowded the new blue / claret / teal leads: 3, 9 (teal to magenta), 11 (steel to cornflower), 20 (teal to olive).

narrative.overview:
A 20th-century broadsheet operated as a scientific instrument. The site is a scholarly database — LLM sentiment models, LDA topics, embeddings, IIIF — that carries the visual grammar of the newspapers it preserves: masthead wordmark, uppercase section strip, thick 2px ink rules, datelines, ledger-style result rows, a press collage printed on a blue plate. The execution is a modern broadsheet's digital archive run by a university press: newspaper typographic conventions with Linear/Stripe-grade product polish.

Ink is the brand; blue is the spot colour. A broadsheet prints in black and adds one second plate where it matters, and since 2.33 the system does exactly that: square corners, no elevation on the page, no cards — sections divided by rules on one flat `--surface` — and a deep press blue used the way a second plate is used. It replaced a burnt orange on rounded, shadowed cards with tracked uppercase labels everywhere, which together read as a generic template product rather than an archive.

Density is a feature, not a compromise: researchers want more items per screen, flat ledger rows over boxed cards, metadata flowing inline with interpunct separators, short prose flowing into newspaper columns rather than sitting in a capped measure. Restraint is the resting state — the quiet control is the default and loudness opts in. Confirmed anti-references: not a small museum's website, not a warm editorial magazine, not a generic dashboard, not a SaaS card grid; no cream or parchment, no pastiche of aged paper.

The system is enforced, not merely written down. Every value the token generator publishes is compared by a guard in this repo and in both consumer modules; a rule that lives only in prose is a rule that has already drifted. That doctrine — publish it and assert it — is why the palette below includes the twenty categorical chart slots and the eleven resource-type and entity hues.
keyCharacteristics: Ink and one spot colour: a deep press blue, used where a second plate would be
Square and flat: zero radii, no shadows on the page, rules instead of boxes
Newspaper grammar (rules, datelines, ledgers, columns) executed with product-grade polish
Uppercase rationed to the nav strip and datelines; every other label is sentence case
Near-white light mode; warm "lamplit reading room" dark mode, declared in full as a mixin pair

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: The press plate — a grayscale collage multiplied over a blue ground built from the raw seed, through a 4px halftone dot screen — is the one big colour statement. It prints twice: as the homepage hero, and at band height as the plate page head of section pages. Everything else earns blue only as an accent. The ground is built from `--primary-base`, never `--primary`, so the plate stays deep blue in dark mode.

rules.name: The Spot-Not-Paint Rule
rules.body: Blue marks what is live or current — links, focus, active state, interpunct, dot, count, the one loud button, the plate. It is never heading text, running prose, a badge fill, a tab fill, or a wash laid for atmosphere. Contrast is not the limit (it clears 10:1); the second plate is. The seed is admin-configurable, so a use that only works because of this particular blue is a use to avoid.

rules.name: The Dot-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Category is a dot on an outlined chip, never a filled or pastel badge. Ten filled badges per screen is shouting; ten dots is an index.

rules.name: The Data-Only Secondary Rule
rules.body: The claret exists for data. If it appears on a button, link, or focus ring, it is a bug.

rules.name: The Mirror-Both-Blocks Rule
rules.body: A custom property is substituted at computed-value time on the element that *declares* it, so a token whose value contains `var(…)` must be declared in **both** theme blocks, and the rule runs both directions. A light-only composition is inherited frozen by every dark descendant; a dark-only declaration leaves a manual light choice on a dark-OS machine unable to win back. The light and dark token blocks are a **mixin pair** carrying the same names, and `npm run check:tokens` asserts it.

rules.name: The Three-to-One Mark Rule
rules.body: Every categorical mark — each `--series-*` slot and each `--type-*` dot — clears 3:1 on all four surfaces of its theme. `npm run check:tokens` measures it; a slot that fails moves in lightness, never in hue.

rules.name: The Published Scale Rule
rules.body: A colour that encodes data belongs in `tokens.json` with a name, a light value and a dark value. Owning a scale means deciding it, never leaving it unpublished in a consumer's source.

rules.name: The Rationed Capitals Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase belongs to two places only, and is set in `--font-condensed` in both: the nav strip (and the drawer that mirrors it) and datelines. Every other label — metadata `dt`s, breadcrumbs, table headers, filter chips, hero stat captions, pagination, form labels, buttons, disclosure toggles — is sentence case, untracked, weight 600 where it is a label.

rules.name: The Slab Tracking Rule
rules.body: Besley display sizes track at -0.01em (`--tracking-display`), never the full -0.02em — slab serifs clog at tight tracking.

rules.name: The Lining Zero Rule
rules.body: Besley's `tnum` zero is broken (frozen at 55 units across weights); use `font-feature-settings: "lnum"` for aligned numerals, never `tabular-nums` with the display serif. All headings set `"kern" "liga" "dlig" "lnum"`.

rules.name: The No-14px Rule
rules.body: The type scale deliberately skips 14px; 11px (`--text-2xs`) is the floor. Absolute `font-size` literals fail `npm run check:tokens`, inside `clamp()`, `min()` and `max()` included — a fluid size composes `--text-*` steps. A weight the theme does not load (Besley 700) fails it too.

rules.name: The Narrow-Space Figure Rule
rules.body: Thousands group with U+202F (narrow no-break space) in every locale — pagination, hero figures and transcript word counts all pass through `number_format($n, 0, '.', "\u{202F}")`. The decimal mark follows the page locale, never the browser's (`12,5 %` fr, `12.5%` en), and date-only values format in UTC.

rules.name: The Bound Punctuation Rule
rules.body: French sets a space before `: ; ! ?` and `»` and after `«`. Titles pass through the `FrenchSpacing` helper, which rewrites those spaces to U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE — same gap, no line break before an orphaned colon.

rules.name: The Fill-the-Width Rule
rules.body: Prose never sits in a narrow capped column with an empty half beside it. Short prose (an HTML block under ~2,400 characters with no table, figure, embed or numbered list; the AI summary on an item) flows into balanced newspaper columns from 1024px — 28rem column width, `--space-10` gap, a 1px `--border` column rule, headings spanning all columns. Long prose stays one column at the full container width; phones get one column. `helper/ProseColumns.php` decides.

rules.name: The One-Spelling Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: `min-width` sits on a published breakpoint and `max-width` at breakpoint − 1px (`#{$md - 1px}`), never Bootstrap's − 0.02px — carrying both idioms in files that reflow the same header is how the halves of a pair both match. Guards in this repo and in both consumer modules assert it, including `matchMedia()` strings and `media=""` attributes.

rules.name: The Separator-Ends-The-Line Rule
rules.body: An inline separator between repeated values is drawn with `::after` on the preceding value, never `::before` on the following one, so a wrap never opens a line on an interpunct that reads as a bullet.

rules.name: The Square-and-Flat Rule
rules.body: `--radius-sm/md/lg` are 0 and the page casts no shadow. A new component that needs a corner or a lift to read as a unit is asking for a rule instead.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: `--shadow-lg` is for things that float over the page and dismiss — drawer, menu, popover, tooltip, typeahead. A panel in the flow never takes it.

rules.name: The Glass Once Rule
rules.body: Backdrop-filter belongs to the sticky header and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Boxes Rule
rules.body: Before adding a card, try a 2px ink rule or a hairline. Boxes are a last resort for true panels (charts). The AI lede, the linked-resources filter bar, the transcript disclosure and every page block were boxes once and are rules now.

rules.name: The Outline-First Focus Rule
rules.body: `--focus-outline` at 2px offset is the focus indicator. The `--ring-focus` halo is the exception for inputs and clipped controls — paired with `outline: 2px solid transparent`, never `outline: none`, so forced-colors mode repaints a real outline. The one legal `outline: none` is `:focus:not(:focus-visible)`. On the plate, focus rings are white.

rules.name: The Two-Switch Rule
rules.body: Page-level tab sets are ruled tabs; in-panel toggles are outlined square chips with a primary border and wash when active. Neither is ever a filled-primary active state — the brand fill belongs to the one loud action — and `--radius-full` is for dots, thumbs and circular icon controls, never a tab or toggle.

rules.name: The Mask-Not-Font Icon Rule
rules.body: A new glyph is a Lucide SVG in `asset/img/` behind `@include icon-mask(url, $forced)`, with `ButtonText` inside buttons and `LinkText` inside links. A rule that sets `background-color` after the mixin re-hides the glyph; set `color`.

dos: **Do** open sections with 2px ink rules and divide rows and columns with hairlines — typography is the architecture, rules are the joinery.
**Do** keep every corner square and every in-flow surface shadowless; reserve `--shadow-lg` for overlays.
**Do** flow short prose into balanced columns at wide viewports and let long prose take the full container width.
**Do** declare every composed or aliased token in **both** theme blocks.
**Do** publish any colour that encodes data as a named light/dark pair in `tokens.json`, and let the guards compare it.
**Do** time motion from `--duration-fast/base/slow` (150 / 200 / 300ms), alone or as `--transition-*` on `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`.
**Do** mark AI-generated fields with the EU "AI GENERATED" provenance treatment on the label, and open the lede on an ink rule.
**Do** mix colours `in oklab`, derive primary variants from the seed, build the plate from `--primary-base`, and run `npm run check:tokens` before trusting any token name.
**Do** test any new font against `ḥ ṣ ḍ ṭ ẓ ʿ ā ī ū` before adopting it.
**Do** give every interactive element a visible focus state — `--focus-outline` first — and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** round a corner or lift a panel, card or button with a shadow or glow.
**Don't** set tracked uppercase anywhere but the nav strip and datelines.
**Don't** put prose in a capped measure with an empty half beside it.
**Don't** use warm cream or parchment surfaces — wrong register ("manuscript museum brochure").
**Don't** add atmospheric gradients, gradient bars, glassmorphism (outside the sticky header), or coloured side-stripes.
**Don't** give a tab or toggle a filled-primary active state, or a pill shape.
**Don't** fill category badges, colour headings, or paint washes in the spot blue — category is a dot, blue is a second plate.
**Don't** use cold blue-gray dark surfaces — dark mode is warm ("lamplit"), hue ~70–80.
**Don't** box result rows, filter bars, linked-resource lists, page blocks or the AI lede into cards.
**Don't** replace an outline focus indicator with the `--ring-focus` halo for convenience, and never with `outline: none` alone.
**Don't** use bouncing/elastic easing or hover-triggered hero animations (the one-time Ken Burns settle is the sanctioned exception; the plate page head has no animation).
**Don't** pair Besley with `tabular-nums` (broken tnum zero) or track it tighter than -0.01em.
**Don't** write an absolute `font-size` literal, inside `clamp()` included, or spell the "below" half of a breakpoint pair any way but breakpoint − 1px.
